title: skill-compiler: compile skills into validated cached adapters, with pool-attested pass verification
body: Port of fork PR 12 (the contributor's fork) onto current upstream/main. Rebuilt in a worktree by cherry-picking only the branch's own commits, so it carries none of the fork main's history. Own test suites run locally and pass on the branch. Companion upstream PRs replace the fifteen fork PRs that were opened in the wrong place.
source: On 2026-10-22 the maintainer delegated the review loop to agents, including judging findings. Codex assessed all 80 artifact findings and the original gpt-6-astra review session independently checked them with source inspection and focused synthetic reproductions. Judgments are delegated agent decisions, not individually confirmed maintainer labels. The review used the PR merge-base shown here; integration was checked against main eab04ad4097fb2030f27bee6026e24f57289f12d. GitHub reports no PR body edit history. The body has identifying names generalized as in the earlier case. The published evaluation is https://github.com/laude-institute/headlong/pull/156#issuecomment-6339258666. The repair is a6a3feb5680b41e3cabe7deaa1fafe185b20c037. Optional findings remain deferred; no merge or approval was made.

findings.label: invalid
findings.what: History harvest leaks operator credentials into the teacher prompt from unrelated trajectories. harvest_history_pool runs on auto-harvest by default (SKILL_AUTO_HARVEST unset) and greps every *.jsonl under the live trajectory dir for the skill script name, with no BAD-pattern filter applied to the `cmd` field it captures. Any reasoning row whose command mentions the script is treated as an invocation, and on `python3 probe.py | jq` or `curl -H "Authorization: $OPENROUTER_API_KEY" .../probe.py` the pending cmd is stored; when no later shell-output row pairs with it, entries collected. The teacher prompt then embeds those history lines (the pool), so an unrelated operator's command lines and tokens inside them go to the third-party teacher model provider. The line filter `BAD` is only applied to stdout, never to cmd.

found_by.text: skill-compiler writes every runner's forwarding API keys and full trajectory content into persistent world-readable reports. The compile path exports the credential keys from the operator `.env` (OPENROUTER_API_KEY etc.) into the `shellm` runner's environment, then persists that run's records. `write_cache` (lines 1287-1536) writes `.json`, `.md` and `.prov` into `$COMPILED_DIR` (default `<state-home>/skill-compiler/compiled`) using `open(...)` with the default umask, without any mode restriction, and the per-run dirs are kept if `SC_KEEP_RUNS=1`. The report's `.prov`/`.md` files also echo every `expect_contains` literal and the final answer from the trajectory. Anyone with read access to the state home (other local users on a shared box, or a backup of `~/.headlong`) can read the API keys harvested from the environment. The README states `.env` is never copied into the workdir, but doesn't mention credential exposure in reports.

findings.label: invalid
findings.what: expect_contains is never checked after a successful runner when the case has literals but `pass` was set by a subprocess-heavy path. The literal loop runs only when `$pass == true`, and it is entered only when at least one literal exists. That part is consistent, but the evidence extraction at line 967 uses `_sc_jq -rs ... || true`; on an empty/absent `$actual_traj_file` (which is forced empty by the root-selection failure path but also allowed when no harness error was set) the whole check silently yields empty content, every literal is reported as missed, and this is indistinguishable from a real miss. Prior to that, when `harness_error` is set but the jq expressions at lines 933-935 fail, `last_step_type` becomes the jq error text rather than empty. This conflates a harness fault with a genuine assertion failure and the summary cannot be trusted. More importantly, when the runner *succeeds* but the trajectory contains no evidence rows, `exec_content` is empty, so `expect_contains_missed` is populated even though no evidence was scanned rather than `expect_contains_unchecked`.

findings.label: invalid
findings.what: Overriding TMPDIR at startup breaks every mktemp and the runs base when the scratch tree is cleaned. Line 13 exports TMPDIR=$SC_SCRATCH for the whole process, and execute_test later reassigns it to the per-test $rundir (line 861). The scratch and each rundir are removed by cleanup (line 22-27) and cmd_compile never restores TMPDIR between tests, so any later mktemp into the removed path (e.g. _sc_src_pool_py, `_sc_jq` staging files at line 86 — no `|| return 1` fallback there) fails. More immediately, `runs_base="${SC_RUNS_BASE:-$SC_SCRATCH/runs-data}"` recreates scratch data under a directory that cleanup deletes as a whole, and the `mktemp -d "$SC_TMP_BASE/run.XXXXXX"` at line 12 runs before the state home exists? No — `mkdir -p "$SC_TMP_BASE"` at line 11 creates it. The defect is that the user-facing `TMPDIR` inheritance documented nowhere is silently replaced, so unrelated tools (llm, skills, shellm probes) write into the scratch dir that is deleted on exit, including when SC_KEEP_RUNS is set and users expect the retained runs only.

findings.label: invalid
findings.what: write_cache overwrites an explicit SKILL_REAL_OUTPUT with the auto-harvested history cache. In write_cache, `real_out_src` is set to the history harvest cache path via `harvest_history_pool "$skill_dir"` and then exported as `SKILL_REAL_OUTPUT="${real_out_src:-}"` (line 1127). That replaces the operator's SKILL_REAL_OUTPUT with an auto-harvested history file whenever the operator did not set SKILL_HISTORY_POOL, so a literal that appears in old trajectory output is labelled TOOL-OUTPUT even though the operator asked to classify against their own capture. The commit comment at 1108-1112 says SKILL_REAL_OUTPUT and SKILL_HISTORY_POOL 'win when set', but only SKILL_HISTORY_POOL's file is actually passed through; an operator-supplied SKILL_REAL_OUTPUT is overwritten whenever harvest succeeds. The harvest file also carries `script`, `pool`, and other metadata strings, which `_collect_strings` only partly filters (it walks `entries`, but a plain-text fallback adds every line), so metadata can be reported as TOOL-OUTPUT.
